projects.name: Digital to Physical
projects.summary: A private, client-side tool that turns digital comic archives into print-ready PDFs with spread alignment, booklet padding, flexible back covers and a live pre-print audit.

projects.name: Graphite Message Lab
projects.summary: A public message form with private-by-default moderation, backed by Django, PostgreSQL, Redis and Celery and deployed automatically through the Project Graphite hosting path.

showcase.problem: Project Graphite needed an approachable application that visitors could use while proving the complete path from a browser through an API, persistent database and background worker.
showcase.approach: Visitors submit public or private messages through Django. PostgreSQL stores them, Redis and Celery process them asynchronously, and moderation keeps messages private until an admin chooses to publish them. Coolify redeploys the Compose application when the main branch changes.
showcase.outcome: The live lab demonstrates routing, TLS, application health, persistence, asynchronous work, administrator review and automatic deployment through one interaction visitors can understand.

contributions.summary: Defined the test scenario and owns the deployment, infrastructure and acceptance criteria used to validate the Graphite hosting path.

projects.name: Graphite Tracker
projects.summary: A universal entertainment tracker for movies, television, anime, manga, manhwa and games.

showcase.problem: Films, series, anime, manga and games are usually tracked in separate apps, so a reader's progress, ratings and upcoming releases end up split across several services.
showcase.approach: One NestJS API pulls TMDB, MangaDex and IGDB or RAWG data into a shared catalogue and a library with per-category progress. Readers import Mihon and AniYomi backups, rate and review finished titles, and get in-app and email alerts for new episodes, chapters and releases. Adult content stays filtered unless a reader opts in.
showcase.outcome: A live, phone-ready tracker where one account holds every category's library, progress, reviews and release alerts, behind a public or private profile and administrator moderation.

contributions.summary: Designed and built the NestJS API, Prisma data model, React frontend, source integrations, backup import, release notifications and moderation, and owns the CI and Coolify deployment.

projects.name: Graphite UI
projects.summary: The shared Project Graphite design tokens, dark theme and React components used by every Graphite web app.

projects.name: PixelPocket
projects.summary: Play Game Boy games in your browser. A custom C++ Game Boy emulator compiled to WebAssembly, with a React frontend and a Node.js API.

showcase.problem: Playing Game Boy games usually means installing and configuring a desktop emulator, and save files stay stuck on the machine they were made on. There was no simple way to pick a game from a library, play it in the browser on any device and keep the same progress.
showcase.approach: A Game Boy (DMG) emulator written from scratch in C++20 (CPU, graphics, sound, timers and MBC1/MBC3/MBC5 cartridges), compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten and run inside a React app with Web Audio sound and keyboard, gamepad and touch input. An Express API on MongoDB and MinIO handles accounts, the game library, uploads and battery saves, checking ROM headers and re-encoding cover images before storing them. Docker Compose runs the stack.
showcase.outcome: Visitors pick a game and play it right on the page, with no install and no server round-trip during play, and signed-in players' saves follow them to any device. The core passes all 11 of Blargg's cpu_instrs tests and renders dmg-acid2 correctly.

contributions.summary: Built the whole platform: the C++ emulator core and its WebAssembly build, the React frontend, the Express API with its storage, and the Docker Compose deployment.

projects.name: StackSwitch
projects.summary: A Windhawk taskbar launcher that starts and stops configurable working sets of applications, folders, editor workspaces, URLs and terminal commands with one action.

showcase.problem: A development session can mean opening the same mix of applications, workspaces, folders, URLs and terminal commands, then finding and closing them all again in the right order.
showcase.approach: StackSwitch adds a native taskbar panel with persistent selections, named profiles, grouped items, launch delays and wait-for-exit behavior. It closes the same selection in reverse order and avoids fragile Windows symbol resolution by using a layered child window.
showcase.outcome: One taskbar action can start or stop a repeatable working environment while optional tools stay disabled until needed.

contributions.summary: Designed and implemented the Win32 taskbar integration, configuration model, process orchestration, profiles, persisted selections and user-facing launcher panel.

projects.name: TaskTune
projects.summary: A configurable Windhawk media player embedded in the Windows 11 taskbar, with media-session controls, per-app volume, audio-only application support and an optional spectrum visualizer.

showcase.problem: Checking playback details or controlling several media and audio applications usually means opening a player window or a separate volume interface and leaving the current workflow.
showcase.approach: The mod injects a configurable Fluent UI player into the Windows 11 taskbar, reads Windows media sessions, falls back to active audio sessions, and exposes playback, session and per-application volume controls beside an optional WASAPI visualizer.
showcase.outcome: Media status and the most common playback and volume actions remain available at a glance without adding a separate background application or replacing Windows system files.

contributions.summary: Designed and maintains the media-session integration, taskbar player, per-application audio controls, visualizer, customization model and Project Graphite packaging.
